# 🕰️ opencode-chronometer **The agent's sense of time — a wall-clock mark inside every tool result.** [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@tuzelko/opencode-chronometer?style=flat-square&color=CB3837&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tuzelko/opencode-chronometer) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@tuzelko/opencode-chronometer?style=flat-square)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tuzelko/opencode-chronometer) [![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/TuzelKO/opencode-chronometer?style=flat-square)](./LICENSE) [![OpenCode V2](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-V2-5B8DEF?style=flat-square)](https://opencode.ai)
--- An LLM lives in a timeless bubble. The system prompt tells it today's date, but not the current time — and nothing tells it how long a step took. **Chronometer** fixes that by appending the local wall clock to completed tool results, at most once per interval per session. It never interrupts the model. It just leaves a small, durable timestamp in the transcript — a pulse the agent can read. ## 👀 What it looks like ```text [chronometer] 2026-11-04 10:40:32 (Europe/Moscow) ``` One line, appended to a tool result that was about to be written anyway. ## 📦 Install ```sh opencode plugin add @tuzelko/opencode-chronometer ``` Or straight from Git: ```sh opencode plugin add github:TuzelKO/opencode-chronometer ``` Requires OpenCode V2. ## ⚙️ Configure `opencode plugin add` writes a plain string entry. To tune the cadence, replace it with the object form: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "@tuzelko/opencode-chronometer", "options": { "intervalMs": 30000 } } ] } ``` | Option | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `intervalMs` | `number` | `60000` | Minimum gap between marks in one session. Values below `1000` or non-finite fall back to `60000`. | ## 🧠 How it works - Hooks `execute.after` for every completed tool result. - Keeps per-session state, so parallel sessions and subagents each get their own cadence. - Appends the mark to the result's `content`, the field the server persists — so it stays in the transcript instead of poisoning a cache segment with a transient line. - Any failure is swallowed: the tool result always survives. ## 📝 Notes - The timezone is the one of the machine running the OpenCode server. - The mark is plain text; nothing is sent anywhere. ## 📄 License MIT © Eugene Frost
